summary: CoAP module is the deepest of the tranche: /.well-known/core inventory, Observe live telemetry drain, actuator PUT with pre-value rollback (T2 write-proof with safety), DTLS ClientHello parse pulling PSK identity hint + weak-cipher selection, Proxy-Uri open-proxy test, and UDP amplifier ratio. test_write defaults False so actuator PUT is opt-in — reasonable. Biggest gap: no /.well-known/edhoc (RFC 9528) or /.well-known/certauth probe; no OSCORE-context enumeration; DTLS probe stops at ServerHello — doesn't try common PSK IDs like 'Client_identity'/'admin' to attempt a T3 handshake.

findings.tier_evidence: RST/ACK to an empty CON just fingerprints the service.
findings.promotion_notes: Fingerprint-only by design — resource_inventory/observe cover T1+.

findings.title_pattern: CoAP endpoint exposes resource inventory via /.well-known/core
findings.tier_evidence: Unauth GET /.well-known/core → 2.05 + parsed link-format list proves anon inventory read.
findings.promotion_notes: Already partly T2 via resource_sweep (reads every resource). Add: promote sev to critical when actuator-typed resources appear (already done). Detect /.well-known/edhoc, /.well-known/rd (Resource Directory) — RD write attempts land T2 registration hijack.
findings.tester_next_step: coap-client -m get coap://<ip>:5683/.well-known/core; for path in <list>; do coap-client -m get coap://<ip>:5683$path; done.

findings.title_pattern: CoAP endpoint accepts anonymous PUT to an actuator resource
findings.tier_evidence: Real PUT sent, 2.xx response confirmed, rollback attempted with pre-captured value — deterministic proof of physical-world write primitive.
findings.promotion_notes: This IS the initial access on IoT; foothold=controlling the actuator. Wire to a per-device tester note (Shelly relay=0/1, Tasmota POWER, valve position) once vendor known. Already gated on test_write flag — keep that.
findings.tester_next_step: coap-client -m put -e '<pre_value>' coap://<ip>:5683<path> (recce already captured pre_value); operator command example: coap-client -m put -e '1' coap://<ip>:5683/a/light — DO NOT run without written authorization.

findings.title_pattern: CoAP endpoint discloses device identity / firmware via device resource
findings.tier_evidence: Actual GET body pulled (up to 256B snippet) from /oic/d, /oic/p, /device etc. — real vendor/model/firmware bytes captured.
findings.promotion_notes: Parse the CBOR/JSON snippet to extract di (device id), n (name), mnmn (manufacturer), mnmo (model), mnfv (firmware) fields per OCF spec. Feed model+firmware to CVE mapper (iotivity CVEs, ESP-IDF advisories). No new traffic — parse existing snippet.
findings.tester_next_step: coap-client -m get -f 60 coap://<ip>:5683/oic/d | cbor-diag; then searchsploit <vendor> <firmware>.

findings.title_pattern: CoAP endpoint leaks live telemetry via Observe (RFC 7641)
findings.tier_evidence: Observe registered, notification packets captured with payload snippets — live telemetry actually pulled.
findings.promotion_notes: Extend window to observe sensor cycles (30-60s), grep for GPS coords, temperature streams, camera frame counters. Feed into known_devices as telemetry_stream=<path> so a later replay attack can be scripted.
findings.tester_next_step: coap-client -m get -s 60 coap://<ip>:5683<obs-path> | tee loot/coap_obs.txt; grep -E 'lat|lon|temp|volt|amp' loot/coap_obs.txt.

findings.title_pattern: CoAP endpoint acts as an open proxy (Proxy-Uri accepted)
findings.tier_evidence: Proxy-Uri to 192.0.2.1 returned anything other than 5.05/4.05 — proof endpoint interpreted request as proxy.
findings.promotion_notes: Point Proxy-Uri at an internal loopback CoAP resource or an intranet HTTP endpoint (Proxy-Uri http://internal/) and confirm response body echoed back — proves SSRF-class relay reaching internal targets.
findings.tester_next_step: coap-client -m get -P coap://<ip>:5683 coap://127.0.0.1/.well-known/core; then coap-client -m get -P coap://<ip>:5683 http://<internal-ip>/ to test HTTP SSRF pivot.

findings.title_pattern: CoAP endpoint is a viable UDP amplifier
findings.tier_evidence: Real byte-ratio measured (>5x) from a live request/response — deterministic amp characterisation.
findings.promotion_notes: Higher tier requires actually launching a spoofed-source amplification attack — always destructive/illegal. Keep at T1.
findings.tester_next_step: Document ratio only. If in-scope stress test: hping3 --udp --spoof <victim> -s 5683 -p 5683 -d 20 <target> — DO NOT run against internet-reachable hosts.

findings.title_pattern: CoAP-DTLS ServerKeyExchange leaks PSK identity hint
findings.tier_evidence: Real ServerKeyExchange psk_identity_hint bytes parsed from DTLS handshake — probe succeeds only when hint is disclosed.
findings.promotion_notes: Feed hint into a bounded PSK dictionary attack: hint often IS the PSK identity to use (e.g. 'Client_identity'/'admin'/serial). Try common PSKs ('','secretPSK', device serial reversed) via mbedtls_ssl_client PSK.
findings.tester_next_step: openssl s_client -dtls1_2 -psk_identity '<hint>' -psk deadbeefdeadbeef -connect <ip>:5684; then coap-client -u '<hint>' -k '<PSK>' coaps://<ip>/.well-known/core once a PSK candidate is found.

findings.title_pattern: CoAP-DTLS server selected a weak / NULL cipher
findings.tier_evidence: ServerHello cipher_suite parsed and matched against NULL/export table — deterministic.
findings.promotion_notes: Complete a full NULL-cipher handshake and issue a plaintext CoAP GET over the resulting session — proves confidentiality is nil. Requires DTLS session bring-up code.
findings.tester_next_step: openssl s_client -dtls1_2 -cipher 'NULL' -psk_identity '<any>' -psk 00 -connect <ip>:5684; then send a CoAP GET over that channel.

findings.promotion_notes: Covered by dtls_psk_hint / dtls_weak for real signal.
Once known_secrets carry PSK material harvested from other services, retry as coaps:// with each candidate PSK.

findings.tier_evidence: OSCORE Option observed in a reply — fingerprint only.
findings.promotion_notes: OSCORE without the context is opaque; no probe promotes without the master secret.
findings.tester_next_step: coap-client coap://<ip>:5683/.well-known/core; note OSCORE option presence — hunt OSCORE contexts in the enrolling app's binaries.

findings.tier_evidence: Port-number based, no probe result required.
findings.promotion_notes: Pair with on-network sniff: capture any CoAP payload = plaintext IoT telemetry. Requires network position.
findings.tester_next_step: tcpdump -i any -w coap.pcap 'udp port 5683'; tshark -r coap.pcap -Y coap -T fields -e coap.uri_path -e coap.payload.
